1.title: The Genealogy and Birth of Jesus Christ
1.themes: Fulfillment of prophecy, Davidic lineage, Divine origin, Emmanuel (God with us)
1.outline:
I. The Genealogy of Jesus (1:1-17)
II. The Birth of Jesus (1:18-25)
1.summary: Matthew begins his Gospel by tracing the lineage of Jesus back to Abraham and David, establishing his messianic credentials. The narrative then shifts to the miraculous conception of Jesus through the Holy Spirit. An angel appears to Joseph in a dream, reassuring him to take Mary as his wife and revealing that the child will save his people from their sins.

2.title: The Visit of the Magi and the Flight to Egypt
2.themes: Jesus as King of the Jews, Gentile recognition, Hostility to the Messiah, Divine protection, Fulfillment of prophecy
2.outline:
I. The Visit of the Wise Men (2:1-12)
II. The Flight to Egypt (2:13-15)
III. Herod Kills the Children (2:16-18)
IV. The Return to Nazareth (2:19-23)
2.summary: Magi from the East arrive in Jerusalem seeking the newborn King of the Jews, alarming King Herod. Guided by a star, they find Jesus in Bethlehem and worship him. Warned in a dream, they bypass Herod on their return. Joseph is also warned in a dream to flee to Egypt with Mary and Jesus to escape Herod's massacre of the infants. After Herod's death, the holy family settles in Nazareth.

3.title: The Ministry of John the Baptist and the Baptism of Jesus
3.themes: Repentance, The Kingdom of Heaven, Preparation, Trinity, Divine endorsement
3.outline:
I. John the Baptist Prepares the Way (3:1-12)
II. The Baptism of Jesus (3:13-17)
3.summary: John the Baptist preaches repentance in the wilderness of Judea, announcing the imminent arrival of the Kingdom of Heaven and baptizing people in the Jordan River. He sharply rebukes the Pharisees and Sadducees. Jesus comes from Galilee to be baptized by John. As Jesus comes up from the water, the Spirit of God descends like a dove, and a voice from heaven declares him to be God's beloved Son.

4.title: The Temptation of Jesus and the Beginning of His Ministry
4.themes: Temptation, Obedience, Word of God, Kingdom of Heaven, Calling of disciples, Healing
4.outline:
I. The Temptation of Jesus (4:1-11)
II. Jesus Begins His Ministry in Galilee (4:12-17)
III. Jesus Calls the First Disciples (4:18-22)
IV. Jesus Ministers to Great Crowds (4:23-25)
4.summary: Jesus is led by the Spirit into the wilderness, where he fasts for forty days and is tempted by Satan. Jesus defeats each temptation by quoting Scripture. After John is arrested, Jesus begins preaching repentance in Galilee. He calls Peter, Andrew, James, and John to be "fishers of men." His ministry of teaching, preaching, and healing attracts large crowds from various regions.

5.title: The Sermon on the Mount: The Beatitudes and the Higher Righteousness
5.themes: Blessing, Kingdom values, Fulfillment of the Law, True righteousness, Love for enemies
5.outline:
I. The Beatitudes (5:1-12)
II. Salt and Light (5:13-16)
III. Christ Fulfills the Law (5:17-20)
IV. Teaching on Anger, Lust, and Divorce (5:21-32)
V. Teaching on Oaths, Retaliation, and Love for Enemies (5:33-48)
5.summary: Jesus ascends a mountain and begins his most famous discourse, opening with the Beatitudes, which describe the character and blessedness of Kingdom citizens. He calls his followers the salt of the earth and the light of the world. Jesus asserts that he came to fulfill the Law, not abolish it, and then intensifies several Old Testament commands, focusing on the heart's intent regarding anger, lust, divorce, oaths, retaliation, and loving one's enemies.

6.title: The Sermon on the Mount: Authentic Piety and Trust in God
6.themes: Hypocrisy, The Lord's Prayer, Fasting, True treasure, Anxiety, Trusting God's provision
6.outline:
I. Giving to the Needy (6:1-4)
II. The Lord's Prayer (6:5-15)
III. Fasting (6:16-18)
IV. Treasures in Heaven (6:19-24)
V. Do Not Be Anxious (6:25-34)
6.summary: Jesus warns against performing acts of righteousness—giving, praying, and fasting—to be seen by others, teaching instead to do them in secret for God's reward. He provides the Lord's Prayer as a model. He exhorts his followers to lay up treasures in heaven rather than on earth, declaring that one cannot serve both God and money. Finally, he commands them not to worry about basic needs, urging them to seek first God's kingdom and righteousness.

7.title: The Sermon on the Mount: Judgment, Discernment, and the Two Foundations
7.themes: Judging others, Prayer, The Golden Rule, False prophets, True discipleship, Obedience
7.outline:
I. Judging Others (7:1-6)
II. Ask, Seek, Knock (7:7-11)
III. The Golden Rule (7:12)
IV. The Narrow Gate (7:13-14)
V. A Tree and Its Fruit (7:15-20)
VI. I Never Knew You (7:21-23)
VII. Build Your House on the Rock (7:24-29)
7.summary: Jesus concludes the Sermon on the Mount by warning against hypocritical judgment and encouraging persistent prayer. He summarizes the Law and Prophets with the Golden Rule. He describes the narrow gate that leads to life and warns against false prophets, identifiable by their fruit. Emphasizing obedience, he states that not all who say "Lord, Lord" will enter the kingdom. He illustrates his teaching with the parable of the wise and foolish builders, leaving the crowds astonished at his authority.

8.title: Miracles of Healing and Authority over Nature and Demons
8.themes: Authority of Jesus, Compassion, Faith, Discipleship, Messianic power
8.outline:
I. Jesus Cleanses a Leper (8:1-4)
II. The Faith of the Centurion (8:5-13)
III. Jesus Heals Many (8:14-17)
IV. The Cost of Following Jesus (8:18-22)
V. Jesus Calms a Storm (8:23-27)
VI. Jesus Heals Two Men with Demons (8:28-34)
8.summary: Following his sermon, Jesus demonstrates his authority through a series of miracles. He heals a leper, a centurion's paralyzed servant (praising the Gentile's great faith), and Peter's mother-in-law, fulfilling Isaiah's prophecy about bearing diseases. He warns of the cost of discipleship. On the Sea of Galilee, he calms a violent storm with a word, marveling his disciples. In the region of the Gadarenes, he delivers two violent demon-possessed men, sending the demons into a herd of pigs.

9.title: Further Miracles, Forgiveness, and the Call of Matthew
9.themes: Authority to forgive sins, Eating with sinners, Fasting, Healing, Compassion for the lost
9.outline:
I. Jesus Heals a Paralytic (9:1-8)
II. Jesus Calls Matthew (9:9-13)
III. A Question About Fasting (9:14-17)
IV. A Girl Restored to Life and a Woman Healed (9:18-26)
V. Jesus Heals Two Blind Men (9:27-31)
VI. Jesus Heals a Man Unable to Speak (9:32-34)
VII. The Harvest is Plentiful (9:35-38)
9.summary: Jesus heals a paralytic, explicitly claiming the authority to forgive sins. He calls Matthew, a tax collector, to follow him, and defends dining with sinners to the Pharisees. After answering a question about fasting using the analogy of new wineskins, he raises a ruler's daughter from the dead and heals a woman with a bleeding disorder. He also restores sight to two blind men and casts out a mute demon. Moved by compassion for the crowds, he urges prayer for more laborers for the spiritual harvest.

10.title: The Commissioning of the Twelve Apostles
10.themes: Apostolic authority, Mission, Persecution, Fearlessness, Cost of discipleship, Reward
10.outline:
I. The Twelve Apostles (10:1-4)
II. Jesus Sends Out the Twelve (10:5-15)
III. Persecution Will Come (10:16-25)
IV. Have No Fear (10:26-33)
V. Not Peace, but a Sword (10:34-39)
VI. Rewards (10:40-42)
10.summary: Jesus summons his twelve disciples, giving them authority over unclean spirits and diseases. He sends them out to the "lost sheep of Israel" to proclaim the kingdom and heal. He provides detailed instructions, warning them of impending persecution and trials but encouraging them not to fear those who can only kill the body. He emphasizes that loyalty to him must surpass family ties, taking up one's cross, and promises rewards to those who receive his messengers.

11.title: Jesus and John the Baptist; The Yoke of Christ
11.themes: Doubt, Identity of Jesus and John, Unbelief, Judgment, Rest, Revelation
11.outline:
I. Messengers from John the Baptist (11:1-6)
II. Jesus Praises John the Baptist (11:7-19)
III. Woe to Unrepentant Cities (11:20-24)
IV. Come to Me, and I Will Give You Rest (11:25-30)
11.summary: John the Baptist, now imprisoned, sends disciples to ask if Jesus is truly the awaited one. Jesus answers by pointing to his miracles. Jesus praises John as the greatest prophet but notes the generation's rejection of both John's asceticism and Jesus' joyful ministry. He denounces the Galilean cities where he performed many miracles for their lack of repentance. Finally, he praises the Father for revealing truth to the humble and offers his easy yoke and rest to the weary and burdened.

12.title: Sabbath Controversies and the Unpardonable Sin
12.themes: Lord of the Sabbath, Mercy over sacrifice, Blasphemy against the Spirit, Sign of Jonah, True family
12.outline:
I. Jesus Is Lord of the Sabbath (12:1-8)
II. A Man with a Withered Hand (12:9-14)
III. God's Chosen Servant (12:15-21)
IV. Blasphemy Against the Holy Spirit (12:22-32)
V. A Tree Is Known by Its Fruit (12:33-37)
VI. The Sign of Jonah (12:38-42)
VII. Return of an Unclean Spirit (12:43-45)
VIII. Jesus' Mother and Brothers (12:46-50)
12.summary: Conflict with the Pharisees escalates over Sabbath observance when the disciples pluck grain and Jesus heals a man with a withered hand, leading the Pharisees to plot his death. Fulfilling prophecy as God's gentle servant, Jesus heals a demon-oppressed man. When Pharisees attribute his power to Beelzebul, he warns that blasphemy against the Spirit is unforgivable. He refuses to give a sign except the "sign of Jonah" and redefines his family as those who do the will of his Father.

13.title: The Parables of the Kingdom
13.themes: Kingdom of Heaven, Mystery, Receptivity of the heart, Judgment, Hidden treasure
13.outline:
I. The Parable of the Sower (13:1-9, 18-23)
II. The Purpose of Parables (13:10-17)
III. The Parable of the Weeds (13:24-30, 36-43)
IV. The Mustard Seed and the Leaven (13:31-33)
V. Hidden Treasure and the Pearl of Great Value (13:44-46)
VI. The Parable of the Net (13:47-50)
VII. New and Old Treasures (13:51-52)
VIII. Jesus Rejected at Nazareth (13:53-58)
13.summary: Jesus teaches the crowds from a boat using a series of parables about the Kingdom of Heaven. The Parable of the Sower illustrates different responses to the gospel. He explains that parables reveal truth to disciples but hide it from the hard-hearted. Further parables—the Weeds, Mustard Seed, Leaven, Hidden Treasure, Pearl, and Net—describe the kingdom's growth, extraordinary value, and the final judgment separating the righteous from the wicked. He is subsequently rejected in his hometown of Nazareth due to their unbelief.

14.title: The Death of John the Baptist, Feeding the 5,000, and Walking on Water
14.themes: Martyrdom, Divine provision, Miracles, Faith and doubt, Worship
14.outline:
I. The Death of John the Baptist (14:1-12)
II. Jesus Feeds the Five Thousand (14:13-21)
III. Jesus Walks on the Water (14:22-33)
IV. Jesus Heals the Sick in Gennesaret (14:34-36)
14.summary: Herod Antipas mistakenly believes Jesus is a resurrected John the Baptist, whom Herod had recently beheaded at the request of Herodias's daughter. Upon hearing of John's death, Jesus withdraws but is followed by crowds. Moved by compassion, he miraculously feeds 5,000 men (plus women and children) with five loaves and two fish. Later that night, Jesus walks on the Sea of Galilee. Peter briefly walks on water too but sinks due to fear, crying out to be saved. The disciples worship Jesus as the Son of God.

15.title: Tradition and Defilement, and the Faith of a Canaanite Woman
15.themes: Hypocrisy, Purity of heart, Gentile faith, Compassion, Miraculous provision
15.outline:
I. Traditions and Commandments (15:1-9)
II. What Defiles a Person (15:10-20)
III. The Faith of a Canaanite Woman (15:21-28)
IV. Jesus Heals Many (15:29-31)
V. Jesus Feeds the Four Thousand (15:32-39)
15.summary: Jesus rebukes the Pharisees for elevating human tradition above God's commandments, teaching that true defilement comes from wicked thoughts in the heart, not unwashed hands. Withdrawing to Tyre and Sidon, he tests and then rewards the persistent, humble faith of a Canaanite woman by healing her demon-oppressed daughter. Returning near the Sea of Galilee, he heals many and miraculously feeds a crowd of 4,000 men (plus women and children) from seven loaves and a few fish.

16.title: Peter's Confession and Jesus' Prediction of His Death
16.themes: Signs, Leaven of the Pharisees, Revelation of the Messiah, The Church, Suffering, Discipleship
16.outline:
I. The Pharisees and Sadducees Demand a Sign (16:1-4)
II. The Leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees (16:5-12)
III. Peter Confesses Jesus as the Christ (16:13-20)
IV. Jesus Foretells His Death and Resurrection (16:21-23)
V. Take Up Your Cross and Follow Jesus (16:24-28)
16.summary: Jesus refuses a sign to the Pharisees and Sadducees, warning his disciples against their "leaven" (teaching). At Caesarea Philippi, Peter makes the foundational confession that Jesus is "the Christ, the Son of the living God." Jesus blesses Peter, promising to build his church. Immediately after, Jesus plainly predicts his impending suffering, death, and resurrection. When Peter objects, Jesus strongly rebukes him. Jesus then outlines the cost of discipleship: denying oneself, taking up one's cross, and following him.

17.title: The Transfiguration and the Healing of a Boy with a Demon
17.themes: Divine glory, The Law and Prophets, Faith, Passion prediction, Temple tax
17.outline:
I. The Transfiguration (17:1-13)
II. Jesus Heals a Boy with a Demon (17:14-21)
III. Jesus Again Foretells Death, Resurrection (17:22-23)
IV. The Temple Tax (17:24-27)
17.summary: Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain where he is transfigured in glory, appearing with Moses and Elijah. The Father's voice commands them to listen to his beloved Son. Descending, Jesus explains that "Elijah" has already come in the person of John the Baptist. He then heals a demon-possessed boy whom the disciples could not cure, attributing their failure to little faith. Jesus again predicts his death, and later miraculous provides a coin from a fish's mouth to pay the temple tax.

18.title: Discourse on the Church: Humility, Sin, and Forgiveness
18.themes: Humility, Care for little ones, Church discipline, Forgiveness, Grace
18.outline:
I. Who Is the Greatest? (18:1-6)
II. Temptations to Sin (18:7-9)
III. The Parable of the Lost Sheep (18:10-14)
IV. If Your Brother Sins Against You (18:15-20)
V. The Parable of the Unforgiving Servant (18:21-35)
18.summary: In a discourse on relationships within the Kingdom, Jesus teaches that true greatness requires humility like that of a child, and severely warns against causing "little ones" to stumble. He illustrates God's care for every believer with the Parable of the Lost Sheep. He provides a procedure for addressing sin in the church (church discipline). Prompted by Peter's question on forgiveness, Jesus tells the Parable of the Unforgiving Servant, stressing that those forgiven immense debts by God must forgive others.

19.title: Teachings on Divorce, Children, and Wealth
19.themes: Marriage, Divorce, Celibacy, Childlike faith, Riches, Eternal life, Rewards
19.outline:
I. Teaching About Divorce (19:1-12)
II. Let the Children Come to Me (19:13-15)
III. The Rich Young Man (19:16-30)
19.summary: Jesus travels to Judea where Pharisees test him on divorce. He affirms God's original design for lifelong marriage, allowing divorce only for sexual immorality, and discusses celibacy. He welcomes little children, laying hands on them and declaring the kingdom belongs to such as these. A rich young man asks how to get eternal life but walks away sorrowful when told to sell his possessions, prompting Jesus to teach on the danger of wealth and the promised rewards for his followers.

20.title: The Parable of the Laborers and the Journey to Jerusalem
20.themes: Grace, Equality of reward, Suffering, Servant leadership, Healing
20.outline:
I. Laborers in the Vineyard (20:1-16)
II. Jesus Foretells His Death a Third Time (20:17-19)
III. A Mother's Request (20:20-28)
IV. Jesus Heals Two Blind Men (20:29-34)
20.summary: Jesus tells the Parable of the Laborers in the Vineyard, illustrating God's sovereign grace where the last shall be first and equal reward is given regardless of time served. Heading toward Jerusalem, Jesus predicts his crucifixion for a third time. The mother of James and John requests places of honor for her sons, prompting Jesus to teach that true greatness in his kingdom comes through serving and giving one's life as a ransom. Leaving Jericho, he heals two blind men who cry out for mercy.

21.title: The Triumphal Entry and Controversies in the Temple
21.themes: Messianic king, Cleansing the temple, Authority, Rejection, Judgment on Israel
21.outline:
I. The Triumphal Entry (21:1-11)
II. Jesus Cleanses the Temple (21:12-17)
III. Jesus Curses the Fig Tree (21:18-22)
IV. The Authority of Jesus Challenged (21:23-27)
V. The Parable of the Two Sons (21:28-32)
VI. The Parable of the Tenants (21:33-46)
21.summary: Jesus enters Jerusalem riding on a donkey, fulfilling Zechariah's prophecy, while crowds praise him as the Son of David. He cleanses the temple, overturning the money changers' tables. The next day, he curses a barren fig tree as an object lesson on faith. In the temple, the religious leaders challenge his authority. Jesus responds with questions and parables—the Two Sons and the Tenants—that indict the leaders for rejecting God's messengers and eventually God's own Son, transferring the kingdom to others.

22.title: Parables, Traps, and the Greatest Commandment
22.themes: Kingdom invitation, Rejection, Taxes, Resurrection, The Greatest Commandment, David's Lord
22.outline:
I. The Parable of the Wedding Feast (22:1-14)
II. Paying Taxes to Caesar (22:15-22)
III. Sadducees Ask About the Resurrection (22:23-33)
IV. The Great Commandment (22:34-40)
V. Whose Son Is the Christ? (22:41-46)
22.summary: Jesus tells the Parable of the Wedding Feast, illustrating the rejection of God's invitation by Israel's leaders and the inclusion of both good and bad, while warning against entering without the proper "wedding garment." The Pharisees and Herodians try to trap him regarding taxes to Caesar, but he answers wisely. The Sadducees question him about the resurrection, which he defends from Scripture. He summarizes the Law into loving God and loving neighbor. Finally, Jesus silences his critics by asking how David can call the Messiah "Lord."

23.title: Seven Woes to the Scribes and Pharisees
23.themes: Hypocrisy, Pride, False teaching, Judgment, Lament over Jerusalem
23.outline:
I. A Warning Against Hypocrisy (23:1-12)
II. Seven Woes to the Scribes and Pharisees (23:13-36)
III. Lament over Jerusalem (23:37-39)
23.summary: Jesus addresses the crowds and disciples, warning them against the hypocrisy and pride of the scribes and Pharisees, who preach but do not practice, and seek honor for themselves. He pronounces seven severe "woes" upon the religious leaders, condemning them for hindering others from the kingdom, misplaced priorities, inner corruption while maintaining outward purity, and persecuting the prophets. He concludes with a heartbreaking lament over Jerusalem's impending desolation due to their rejection of him.

24.title: The Olivet Discourse: Signs of the End of the Age
24.themes: Destruction of the temple, Tribulation, Second Coming, Watchfulness, Judgment
24.outline:
I. Jesus Foretells Destruction of the Temple (24:1-2)
II. Signs of the End of the Age (24:3-14)
III. The Abomination of Desolation (24:15-28)
IV. The Coming of the Son of Man (24:29-31)
V. The Lesson of the Fig Tree (24:32-35)
VI. No One Knows That Day and Hour (24:36-51)
24.summary: Leaving the temple, Jesus predicts its total destruction. On the Mount of Olives, the disciples ask about the signs of his coming and the end of the age. Jesus outlines a period of wars, famines, and intense persecution, referring to the "abomination of desolation." He describes his glorious, visible return (the coming of the Son of Man) to gather the elect. Because the exact time is unknown, he stresses the absolute necessity for his followers to remain watchful, ready, and faithful.

25.title: The Olivet Discourse: Parables of Readiness and the Final Judgment
25.themes: Preparation, Stewardship, Final Judgment, Sheep and goats, Eternal destiny
25.outline:
I. The Parable of the Ten Virgins (25:1-13)
II. The Parable of the Talents (25:14-30)
III. The Final Judgment (25:31-46)
25.summary: Jesus continues the Olivet Discourse with parables emphasizing readiness. The Parable of the Ten Virgins contrasts wise preparation with foolish negligence. The Parable of the Talents teaches that believers must faithfully steward what God has entrusted to them until he returns. Finally, Jesus depicts the final judgment, where the Son of Man will separate the nations like sheep and goats, based on how they treated "the least of these" his brothers, resulting in eternal punishment or eternal life.

26.title: The Plot, The Last Supper, Gethsemane, and the Arrest
26.themes: Betrayal, Passover, New Covenant, Agony, Submission to the Father's will, Arrest, Trial
26.outline:
I. The Plot to Kill Jesus and the Anointing at Bethany (26:1-13)
II. Judas to Betray Jesus (26:14-16)
III. The Passover and the Lord's Supper (26:17-29)
IV. Jesus Foretells Peter's Denial (26:30-35)
V. Jesus Prays in Gethsemane (26:36-46)
VI. Betrayal and Arrest of Jesus (26:47-56)
VII. Jesus Before Caiaphas and the Council (26:57-68)
VIII. Peter Denies Jesus (26:69-75)
26.summary: As the leaders plot his death, a woman anoints Jesus in Bethany, an act he defends as preparation for burial. Judas agrees to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver. Jesus eats the Passover meal with his disciples, instituting the Lord's Supper. He predicts Peter's denial. In Gethsemane, Jesus agonizes in prayer, submitting to the Father's will. Judas arrives with an armed crowd to arrest him. Jesus is tried before the high priest Caiaphas, mocked, and beaten, while outside in the courtyard, Peter denies him three times.

27.title: The Trial, Crucifixion, and Burial of Jesus
27.themes: Innocence, Atonement, Substitution, Suffering, Death, Burial
27.outline:
I. Jesus Delivered to Pilate and the Death of Judas (27:1-10)
II. Jesus Before Pilate (27:11-26)
III. Jesus Is Mocked (27:27-31)
IV. The Crucifixion (27:32-44)
V. The Death of Jesus (27:45-56)
VI. Jesus Is Buried (27:57-61)
VII. The Guard at the Tomb (27:62-66)
27.summary: Jesus is handed over to Pilate. Judas, filled with remorse, hangs himself. Despite recognizing Jesus' innocence, Pilate bows to the crowd's demand to release Barabbas and crucify Jesus. Soldiers brutally mock and scourge Jesus before leading him to Golgotha. Jesus is crucified between two robbers. Darkness covers the land, and Jesus dies, accompanied by an earthquake and the tearing of the temple curtain. Joseph of Arimathea buries him in a new tomb, which the religious leaders secure with a seal and a Roman guard.

28.title: The Resurrection and the Great Commission
28.themes: Resurrection, Victory over death, Deception, Authority, The Great Commission
28.outline:
I. The Resurrection (28:1-10)
II. The Report of the Guard (28:11-15)
III. The Great Commission (28:16-20)
28.summary: On Sunday morning, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary find the tomb empty; an angel rolls away the stone and announces that Jesus is risen. Jesus appears to the women, instructing them to tell the brothers to go to Galilee. Meanwhile, the religious leaders bribe the guards to lie and say the disciples stole the body. In Galilee, the resurrected Jesus appears to the eleven disciples, claiming all authority and commissioning them to make disciples of all nations, promising his presence to the end of the age.
